title: Secure Links and Embedded Content
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of secure links and embedded content in a browser document.
Apply at least one relevant rule from this lesson to a small HTML example.
Check the result using browser inspection, a validator, or an accessibility checklist.

content.intro: This lesson turns “Secure Links and Embedded Content” into a practical authoring skill. You will work with safe external links, understand the choices that matter, and check the result instead of relying on guesswork.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding browser behavior and boundaries helps you reason about embedded content, interaction, privacy, and how document markup participates in a larger application.

content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: Understanding browser behavior and boundaries helps you reason about embedded content, interaction, privacy, and how document markup participates in a larger application.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Resolve the URL relative to the current document or base URL. Prefer meaningful link text, test internal paths from each page location, and verify external destinations.

items.title: Safe external links
items.text: Resolve the URL relative to the current document or base URL. Prefer meaningful link text, test internal paths from each page location, and verify external destinations.

items.title: The rel attribute and link security
items.text: The rel attribute: the relationship between the current document and the destination, often used to add security or meaning.

items.title: iframe sandboxing
items.text: Embedded content introduces a separate resource and sometimes a separate browsing context. Confirm the origin, disclose third-party dependencies, and restrict capabilities unless they are required.

items.title: Minimizing embedded-resource permissions
items.text: Embedded content introduces a separate resource and sometimes a separate browsing context. Confirm the origin, disclose third-party dependencies, and restrict capabilities unless they are required.

items.title: External resource trust and privacy
items.text: Choose resource hints and loading behavior from measurement, not habit. Preserve intrinsic dimensions, avoid lazy-loading content needed immediately, and prioritize only genuinely important resources.

items.title: Referrer policies and data exposure
items.text: Referrer policies and data exposure is one of the decisions covered by Secure Links and Embedded Content. Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Avoid using an element or attribute just because its default appearance seems convenient.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Native HTML improves structure and browser feedback, but it does not replace server-side authorization or validation.

content.task: Create a small HTML example that demonstrates secure links and embedded content. Keep the markup minimal, give every element a clear purpose, and inspect the rendered result.
task_acceptance_criteria: Use the relevant concept from Secure Links and Embedded Content.
Keep IDs unique and use valid nesting.
Check the result in a browser and record one finding.
hints: Start with the smallest valid example for secure links and embedded content.
Add one element or attribute at a time, then check the result.
Compare the source and rendered DOM if the behavior surprises you.
content.expected_output: The first two links open local pages when those files exist; the fragment link jumps to the Contact section.

troubleshooting.symptom: The expected content does not appear.
troubleshooting.check: Confirm the file was saved with an .html extension and inspect its path and nesting.
Check the resolved URL and confirm the referenced file or external resource exists and allows the request.

troubleshooting.symptom: The page looks correct but the markup may be invalid.
troubleshooting.check: Run the Nu Html Checker and follow its first relevant diagnostic, then validate again.

common_mistakes.why: The default appearance is not the element’s main meaning and can make navigation or maintenance harder.
common_mistakes.fix: Choose the element that matches the content purpose, then use CSS for presentation.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a browser’s recovery means the source is valid
common_mistakes.why: Browsers often recover from malformed markup, which can hide defects and produce unexpected document structure.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect the rendered DOM and run a validator against the original source.

common_mistakes.why: Missing files, narrow viewports, keyboard access, invalid input, or other states can expose defects.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the expected state plus one realistic edge case and an accessibility path.

summary: Secure Links and Embedded Content is about expressing document structure or behavior intentionally.

Decide what the markup is meant to communicate, choose the native HTML structure that expresses that meaning, and verify the result in a browser or a relevant validation checklist. Verify both markup and behavior; do not infer correctness from appearance alone.
